corpusProfile.structure: episodic chapters following Alice through a sequence of encounters
extractionRisks: Treat person-like animals as characters rather than inventing a creature category
Do not turn every size change into a separate entity

extract:primary-0001-87acee8cf1.summary: Alice follows the White Rabbit down a rabbit-hole, finds a locked hall and garden door, and changes size after drinking from a bottle and eating a cake.
plotBeats: Alice discovers the golden key and garden door
Alice shrinks after drinking from the bottle

entities.name: Alice
entities.summary: A curious girl who follows the White Rabbit underground.
entities.excerpt: Alice was beginning to get very tired

claims.text: Alice follows the White Rabbit into the rabbit-hole.
claims.excerpt: she ran across the field after it

entities.name: White Rabbit
entities.summary: A waistcoat-wearing rabbit whose haste draws Alice underground.
entities.excerpt: a White Rabbit with pink eyes

claims.text: The White Rabbit carries a watch in its waistcoat pocket.

entities.name: Dinah
entities.summary: Alice's cat, whom Alice thinks about while falling.

entities.name: Golden Key
entities.summary: A small key that fits the door leading toward the garden.

entities.name: Drink Me Bottle
entities.summary: A labeled bottle whose contents make Alice shrink.

entities.name: Eat Me Cake
entities.summary: A currant-marked cake Alice eats after becoming too small to reach the key.

relationships.subject: Alice
relationships.excerpt: she ran across the field after it

passages.title: The Rabbit is late
passages.speaker: White Rabbit
passages.context: Alice hears the White Rabbit speak before following it.
passages.significance: The ordinary anxiety expressed by an impossible figure triggers Alice's pursuit.

openQuestions: What is the White Rabbit late for?

extract:primary-0002-89c560d007.summary: Alice grows enormous, questions her identity, frightens away the White Rabbit, and meets a Mouse while swimming in her own pool of tears.
plotBeats: Alice grows to more than nine feet
Alice questions whether she is still herself
The White Rabbit drops its fan and gloves
Alice addresses the Mouse in the pool

entities.name: Alice
entities.summary: A girl whose changing size makes her question her identity.
entities.excerpt: Who in the world am I?

claims.text: Alice creates a pool with her tears.
claims.excerpt: she went on all the same, shedding gallons of tears

entities.name: White Rabbit
entities.summary: The anxious rabbit who mistakes Alice's approach and drops his gloves and fan.

entities.name: Mouse
entities.summary: A swimming Mouse whom Alice asks for a way out of the pool.
entities.excerpt:
O Mouse, do
you know the way out of this pool?

entities.name: Dinah
entities.summary: Alice's cat, whose skill at catching mice offends the Mouse.

relationships.subject: Alice
relationships.excerpt:
O Mouse, do
you know the way out of this pool?

passages.title: The great puzzle
passages.speaker: Alice
passages.text:
Who in the world am I? Ah, that’s
the great puzzle!
passages.context: Alice tests her memory after her body changes size.
passages.significance: The question makes identity, rather than size alone, the chapter's central uncertainty.

openQuestions: How will Alice and the Mouse leave the pool?

extract:primary-0003-c7dce16cd1.summary: The wet animals hold a Caucus-Race, the Dodo awards prizes, and Alice drives the group away by talking about Dinah.
plotBeats: Everyone runs without a fixed course
The Dodo declares everyone a winner
The Mouse leaves after Alice misunderstands its tale

entities.name: Alice
entities.summary: A participant who supplies comfits as prizes and misunderstands the Mouse's tale.
entities.excerpt: Alice had no idea what to do

entities.name: Mouse
entities.summary: A touchy Mouse whose history Alice mistakes for the shape of its tail.
entities.excerpt: Mine is a long and a sad tale!

entities.name: Dodo
entities.summary: A solemn bird who proposes the Caucus-Race and judges its result.

claims.text: The Dodo declares that everyone has won.

entities.name: Caucus-Race
entities.summary: An unstructured race proposed as a way for the wet party to dry off.
entities.excerpt: best thing to get us dry would be a Caucus-race

entities.name: Dinah
entities.summary: Alice's cat, whose hunting habits alarm the gathered animals.

relationships.subject: Dodo
relationships.excerpt: best thing to get us dry would be a Caucus-race

passages.title: Everybody has won
passages.speaker: Dodo
passages.text:
Everybody has won, and all
must have prizes.
passages.context: The Dodo announces the result after the race stops.
passages.significance: The verdict turns the race into a satire of procedure without competition or measure.
